title.en: Volume 96 Biographies 46: Yao Chong, Song Jing

sentences.zh: 姚崇，本名元崇，陜州硤石人也。

translations.literal: Yao Chong, original name Yuanchong, was a native of Xiashi in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, whose original name was Yuanchong, was a native of Xiashi in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父善意，貞觀中，任巂州都督。

translations.literal: His father Shan'yi, during the Zhenguan era, served as military governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan'yi served as military governor of Suizhou during the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 元崇爲孝敬挽郎，應下筆成章舉，授濮州司倉，五遷夏官郎中。

translations.literal: Yuanchong served as a Filial Piety and Mourning Dirge Officer, passed the Immediate Composition on Receiving Brush examination, was appointed Registrar of the Suizhou Revenue Office, and was promoted five times to Director in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchong served as a Filial Piety and Mourning Dirge Officer, passed the "Immediate Composition on Receiving Brush" examination, was appointed registrar of the Suizhou revenue office, and was promoted five times to director in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時契丹寇陷河北數州，兵機填委，元崇剖析若流，皆有條貫。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan invaded and overran several prefectures in Hebei; military affairs piled up, yet Yuanchong analyzed them as though flowing water — each matter had its proper order.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan invaded and overran several prefectures in Hebei. Military affairs piled up, yet Yuanchong analyzed them as though water flowing — every matter had its proper order.

sentences.zh: 則天甚奇之，超遷夏官侍郎，又尋同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Empress Wu thought him extraordinary and promoted him to Vice Minister of Personnel; soon after he also became Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Phoenix Pavilion and Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu thought him extraordinary and promoted him to vice minister of personnel; soon after he also became associate censor-in-chief of the Phoenix Pavilion and minister of state.

sentences.zh: 聖暦初，則天謂侍臣曰：「往者周興、來俊臣等推勘詔獄，朝臣遞相牽引，鹹承反逆，國家有法，朕豈能違。

translations.literal: Early in Shengli, Empress Wu said to her attendants: "In the past Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen and the like investigated imperial edict cases, and court officials repeatedly implicated one another — all confessed to treason. The state has law; how could I violate it?
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengli era, Empress Wu said to her attendants, "In the past Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and the like investigated cases under imperial edict, and court officials repeatedly implicated one another — all confessed to treason. The state has laws; how could I violate them?

sentences.zh: 中間疑有枉濫，更使近臣就獄親問，皆得手狀，承引不虛，朕不以爲疑，即可其奏。

translations.literal: Among them I suspected wrongful excess; I again sent close attendants to the prison to question them in person. All obtained confessions in their own hand; the accusations were not false. I did not doubt it and approved their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Among them I suspected wrongful excess, so I again sent close attendants to the prisons to question them in person. All obtained confessions in their own hand; the accusations were not false. I did not doubt it and approved their memorials.

sentences.zh: 近日周興、來俊臣死後，更無聞有反逆者，然則以前就戮者，不有冤濫耶？」

translations.literal: Since Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen died recently, we have heard no more of treason — were those put to death before not wrongfully killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen died recently, we have heard no more of treason — were those put to death before not wrongfully killed?"

sentences.zh: 元崇對曰：「自垂拱已後，被告身死破家者，皆是枉酷自誣而死。

translations.literal: Yuanchong replied: "Since the Chuigong era, all who were accused and died in ruin of house were wrongfully coerced into false confession.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchong replied, "Since the Chuigong era, all who were accused and died with their families ruined were wrongfully coerced into false confession.

sentences.zh: 告者特以爲功，天下號爲羅織，甚於漢之黨錮。

translations.literal: Accusers did it only for achievement; the whole realm called it 'net-weaving,' worse than the Party Proscription of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers did it only for merit; the whole realm called it 'net-weaving,' worse than the Party Proscription of Han.

sentences.zh: 陛下令近臣就獄問者，近臣亦不自保，何敢輒有動搖？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty sent close attendants to question prisoners, those attendants could not even protect themselves — how dare they stir things up?
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty sent close attendants to question prisoners, those attendants could not even protect themselves — how dare they stir things up?

sentences.zh: 被問者若翻，又懼遭其毒手，將軍張虔勖、李安靜等皆是也。

translations.literal: If the questioned reversed their testimony, they feared poisoned hands — Generals Zhang Qianxun and Li Anjing were among these.
translations.idiomatic: If the questioned reversed their testimony, they feared deadly reprisal — Generals Zhang Qianxun and Li Anjing were among these.

sentences.zh: 賴上天降靈，聖情發寤，誅鋤兇豎，朝廷乂安。

translations.literal: Thanks to Heaven sending down numinous aid and Your Majesty's awakening, evil henchmen were punished and cut down; the court was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Heaven sending down numinous aid and Your Majesty's awakening, evil henchmen were punished and cut down, and the court was at peace.

sentences.zh: 今日已後，臣以微軀及一門百口保見在內外官更無反逆者。

translations.literal: From today onward I pledge with my humble person and my household of a hundred mouths that among officials inside and outside there is no treason.
translations.idiomatic: From today onward I pledge with my humble person and my household of a hundred mouths that among officials inside and outside there will be no treason.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下得告狀，但收掌，不須推問。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty, when denunciations arrive, only take charge of them and do not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, when denunciations arrive, only take charge of them and do not investigate.

sentences.zh: 若後有征驗，反逆有實，臣請受知而不告之罪。」

translations.literal: If afterward evidence appears and treason is real, I accept the crime of knowing and not reporting."
translations.idiomatic: If afterward evidence appears and treason is real, I accept the crime of knowing and not reporting."

sentences.zh: 則天大悅曰：「以前宰相皆順成其事，陷朕爲淫刑之主。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and said: "Former chancellors all went along and made me a ruler of excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and said, "Former chancellors all went along and made me a ruler of excessive punishment.

sentences.zh: 聞卿所説，甚合朕心。」

translations.literal: Hearing what you say, it greatly accords with my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing what you say accords greatly with my heart."

sentences.zh: 其日，遣中使送銀千兩以賜元崇。

translations.literal: That day she sent a palace envoy with a thousand taels of silver to reward Yuanchong.
translations.idiomatic: That day she sent a palace envoy with a thousand taels of silver to reward Yuanchong.

sentences.zh: 時突厥叱利元崇構逆，則天不欲元崇與之同名，乃改爲元之。

translations.literal: At that time Chilie Yuanchong of the Turks plotted rebellion; Empress Wu did not wish Yuanchong to share the name and changed it to Yuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chilie Yuanchong of the Turks plotted rebellion; Empress Wu did not wish Yuanchong to share the name and changed it to Yuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 俄遷鳳閣侍郎，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, still directing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, still directing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 長安四年，元之以母老，表請解職侍養，言甚哀切，則天難違其意，拜相王府長史，罷知政事，俾獲其養。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chang'an, Yuanzhi because his mother was old memorialized to resign office and attend to her; his words were very sorrowful and urgent. Empress Wu found it hard to go against his wish, appointed him chief administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household, removed him from directing state affairs, and enabled him to provide for her.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chang'an, Yuanzhi, because his mother was old, memorialized to resign office and attend to her; his words were very sorrowful and urgent. Empress Wu found it hard to go against his wish, appointed him chief administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household, removed him from directing state affairs, and enabled him to provide for her.

sentences.zh: 其月，又令元之兼知夏官尚書事、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: That month she again ordered Yuanzhi to concurrently serve as Minister of Personnel and Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Phoenix Pavilion, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: That month she again ordered Yuanzhi to concurrently serve as minister of personnel and associate censor-in-chief of the Phoenix Pavilion, third rank.

sentences.zh: 元之上言：「臣事相王，知兵馬不便。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi memorialized: "I serve the Prince of Xiang; knowing military affairs is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi memorialized, "I serve the Prince of Xiang; holding military authority is inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 臣非惜死，恐不益相王。」

translations.literal: It is not that I begrudge death, but I fear it will not benefit the Prince of Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I begrudge death, but I fear it will not benefit the Prince of Xiang."

sentences.zh: 則天深然其言，改爲春官尚書。

translations.literal: Empress Wu deeply approved his words and changed him to Minister of the Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu deeply approved his words and changed him to minister of the Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 是時，張易之請移京城大德僧十人配定州私置寺，僧等苦訴，元之斷停，易之屢以爲言，元之終不納。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi requested transferring ten eminent monks of the capital to a privately established temple in Dingzhou; the monks bitterly appealed, and Yuanzhi halted it. Yizhi repeatedly spoke of it, but Yuanzhi ultimately would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi requested transferring ten eminent monks of the capital to a privately established temple in Dingzhou; the monks bitterly appealed, and Yuanzhi halted it. Yizhi repeatedly spoke of it, but Yuanzhi ultimately would not accept.

sentences.zh: 由是爲易之所譖，改爲司仆卿，知政事如故，使充靈武道大總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was slandered by Yizhi, changed to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, still directing state affairs as before, and sent to serve as grand general of the Lingwu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was slandered by Yizhi, changed to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, still directing state affairs as before, and sent to serve as grand general of the Lingwu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，張柬之、桓彥範等謀誅易之兄弟，適會元之自軍還都，遂預謀，以功封梁縣侯，賜實封二百戸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan and the like plotted to execute the Yizhi brothers; it happened that Yuanzhi returned from the army to the capital and joined the plot; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liang County with two hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and the like plotted to execute the Yizhi brothers; it happened that Yuanzhi returned from the army to the capital and joined the plot; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liang County with two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 則天移居上陽宮，中宗率百官就閤起居，王公已下皆欣躍稱慶，元之獨嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Empress Wu moved to the Shangyang Palace; Emperor Zhongzong led the hundred officials to attend at the gate; from princes and dukes downward all rejoiced and celebrated, but Yuanzhi alone sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu moved to the Shangyang Palace; Emperor Zhongzong led the hundred officials to attend at the gate; from princes and dukes downward all rejoiced and celebrated, but Yuanzhi alone sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 彥範、柬之謂元之曰：「今日豈是啼泣時！

translations.literal: Yanfan and Jianzhi said to Yuanzhi: "Today is surely not the time for weeping!
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan and Jianzhi said to Yuanzhi, "Today is surely not the time for weeping!

sentences.zh: 恐公禍從此始。」

translations.literal: I fear disaster for you will begin from this."
translations.idiomatic: I fear disaster for you will begin from this."

sentences.zh: 元之曰：「事則天歲久，乍此辭違，情發於衷，非忍所得。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi said: "I served Empress Wu for many years; suddenly to part from her this way, the feeling arises from the heart — endurance cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi said, "I served Empress Wu for many years; suddenly to part from her this way, the feeling arises from the heart — endurance cannot obtain it.

sentences.zh: 昨預公誅兇逆者，是臣子之常道，豈敢言功；

translations.literal: Yesterday joining you in executing the traitors was the constant way of a subject; how dare I speak of merit;
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday joining you in executing the traitors was the constant way of a subject; how dare I speak of merit;

sentences.zh: 今辭違舊主悲泣者，亦臣子之終節，緣此獲罪，實所甘心。」

translations.literal: now weeping in parting from my old lord is also a subject's final integrity; if I incur punishment for this, I am truly willing."
translations.idiomatic: now weeping in parting from my old lord is also a subject's final integrity; if I incur punishment for this, I am truly willing."

sentences.zh: 無幾，出爲亳州刺史，轉常州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，召拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，尋遷中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed Minister of War and Associate Director of the Secretariat, Third Rank; soon he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed minister of war and associate director of the Secretariat, third rank; soon he was transferred to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗在東宮，太平公主干預朝政，宋王成器爲閑廄使，岐王範、薛王業皆掌禁兵，外議以爲不便。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; Princess Taiping intervened in court politics; Prince Chengqi of Song was Director of the Imperial Stud; Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue all held forbidden troops; outside opinion held it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; Princess Taiping intervened in court politics; Prince Chengqi of Song was director of the imperial stud; Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue all held forbidden troops; outside opinion held it inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 元之同侍中宋璟密奏請令公主往就東都，出成器等諸王爲刺史，以息人心。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi together with Chief Minister Song Jing secretly memorialized requesting that the princess go to the Eastern Capital and the princes Chengqi and the others be sent out as prefects, to calm people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi together with chief minister Song Jing secretly memorialized requesting that the princess go to the Eastern Capital and that Princes Chengqi and the others be sent out as prefects, to calm people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 睿宗以告公主，公主大怒。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong told the princess; the princess was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong told the princess; the princess was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 玄宗乃上疏以元之、璟等離間兄弟，請加罪，乃貶元之爲申州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong then memorialized that Yuanzhi, Jing and the others had estranged the brothers and requested added punishment; Yuanzhi was demoted to prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong then memorialized that Yuanzhi, Jing, and the others had estranged the brothers and requested added punishment; Yuanzhi was demoted to prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 再轉揚州長史、淮南按察使，爲政簡肅，人吏立碑紀德。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to chief administrator of Yangzhou and inspector of Huainan; his governance was simple and stern, and officials and people erected a stele to record his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to chief administrator of Yangzhou and inspector of Huainan; his governance was simple and stern, and officials and people erected a stele to record his virtue.

sentences.zh: 俄除同州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，玄宗講武在新豐驛，召元之代郭元振爲兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，復遷紫微令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Xinfeng Post, summoned Yuanzhi to replace Guo Yuanzhen as Minister of War and Associate Director of the Secretariat, Third Rank, and again transferred him to Director of the Purple Tenuity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian, Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Xinfeng Post, summoned Yuanzhi to replace Guo Yuanzhen as minister of war and associate director of the Secretariat, third rank, and again transferred him to director of the Purple Tenuity.

sentences.zh: 避開元尊號，又改名崇，進封梁國公。

translations.literal: To avoid the honored Kaiyuan title, he again changed his name to Chong and was advanced to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the honored Kaiyuan title, he again changed his name to Chong and was advanced to Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 固辭實封，乃停其舊封，特賜新封一百戸。

translations.literal: He firmly declined taxable enfeoffment; his old enfeoffment was stopped and he was specially granted a new enfeoffment of a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined taxable enfeoffment; his old enfeoffment was stopped and he was specially granted a new enfeoffment of a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時，公主外戚皆奏請度人爲僧尼，亦有出私財造寺者，富戸強丁，皆經營避役，遠近充滿。

translations.literal: Previously, during Emperor Zhongzong's time, princesses and maternal relatives all memorialized requesting ordination of persons as monks and nuns; there were also those who used private wealth to build temples; wealthy households and strong young men all sought to avoid corvée by such means, and they filled the realm near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, during Emperor Zhongzong's time, princesses and maternal relatives all memorialized requesting ordination of persons as monks and nuns; there were also those who used private wealth to build temples; wealthy households and strong young men all sought to avoid corvée by such means, and they filled the realm near and far.

sentences.zh: 至是，崇奏曰：「佛不在外，求之於心。

translations.literal: At this Chong memorialized: "Buddha is not outside; seek him in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: At this Chong memorialized, "Buddha is not outside; seek him in the heart.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄最賢，無益於全趙；

translations.literal: Fotucheng was most worthy, yet he did not benefit all of Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng was most worthy, yet he did not benefit all of Zhao;

sentences.zh: 羅什多藝，不救於亡秦。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva was most versatile, yet he did not save perishing Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva was most versatile, yet he did not save perishing Qin.

sentences.zh: 何充、苻融，皆遭敗滅；

translations.literal: He Chong and Fu Rong both met defeat and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: He Chong and Fu Rong both met defeat and ruin;

sentences.zh: 齊襄、梁武，未免災殃。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiang of Qi and Emperor Wu of Liang did not escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiang of Qi and Emperor Wu of Liang did not escape calamity.

sentences.zh: 但發心慈悲，行事利益，使蒼生安樂，即是佛身。

translations.literal: Only awaken compassion in the heart, act with benefit and do not do evil — then the Buddha-body is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Only awaken compassion in the heart, act with benefit and do not do evil — then the Buddha-body is complete.

sentences.zh: 何用妄度奸人，令壞正法？」

translations.literal: Why vainly ordain wicked men and let them ruin the true Law?"
translations.idiomatic: Why vainly ordain wicked men and let them ruin the true Law?"

sentences.zh: 上納其言，令有司隱括僧徒，以偽濫還俗者萬二千餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and ordered the relevant offices to investigate monks; more than twelve thousand falsely ordained were returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his words and ordered the relevant offices to investigate monks; more than twelve thousand falsely ordained were returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，山東蝗蟲大起，崇奏曰：「《毛詩》云：『秉彼蟊賊，以付炎火。』

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, locusts rose greatly in Shandong; Chong memorialized: "The Mao Odes says: 'Take up those crop pests and commit them to blazing fire.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, locusts rose greatly in Shandong; Chong memorialized, "The Mao Odes says, 'Take up those crop pests and commit them to blazing fire.'

sentences.zh: 又漢光武詔曰：『勉順時政，勸督農桑，去彼蝗蜮，以及蟊賊。』

translations.literal: Also Emperor Guangwu of Han decreed: 'Exhort compliance with the season's policies, urge and oversee agriculture, remove those locust swarms and those crop pests.'
translations.idiomatic: Also Emperor Guangwu of Han decreed, 'Exhort compliance with the season's policies, urge and oversee agriculture, remove those locust swarms and those crop pests.'

sentences.zh: 此並除蝗之義也。

translations.literal: These are all the meaning of eliminating locusts.
translations.idiomatic: These are all the meaning of eliminating locusts.

sentences.zh: 蟲既解畏人，易爲驅逐。

translations.literal: Insects once fear men are easy to drive away.
translations.idiomatic: Once insects fear men, they are easy to drive away.

sentences.zh: 又苗稼皆有地主，救護必不辭勞。

translations.literal: Also the crops all have landowners; to protect them they surely will not decline labor.
translations.idiomatic: Also the crops all have landowners; to protect them they surely will not decline labor.

sentences.zh: 蝗既解飛，夜必赴火，夜中設火，火邊掘坑，且焚且瘞，除之可盡。

translations.literal: Locusts once know flight, at night surely rush to fire; set fires at night, dig pits beside the fires, burn and bury together — elimination can be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once locusts know flight, at night they surely rush to fire; set fires at night, dig pits beside the fires, burn and bury together — elimination can be complete.

sentences.zh: 時山東百姓皆燒香禮拜，設祭祈恩，眼看食苗，手不敢近。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Shandong all burned incense and bowed, set offerings and prayed for grace, watching crops eaten while hands dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people of Shandong all burned incense and bowed, set offerings and prayed for grace, watching crops eaten while their hands dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 自古有討除不得者，只是人不用命，但使齊心戮力，必是可除。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity there have been cases where extermination could not be achieved — it was only that men did not obey orders; but if they unite heart and join strength, they surely can be eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity there have been cases where extermination could not be achieved — it was only that men did not obey orders; but if they unite heart and join strength, they surely can be eliminated."

sentences.zh: 乃遣御史分道殺蝗。

translations.literal: He then sent censors by separate routes to kill locusts.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent censors by separate routes to kill locusts.

sentences.zh: 汴州刺史倪若水執奏曰：「蝗是天災，自宜修德。

translations.literal: Prefect Ni Ruoshui of Bianzhou submitted a memorial: "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster; one should cultivate virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Ni Ruoshui of Bianzhou submitted a memorial, "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster; one should cultivate virtue.

sentences.zh: 劉聰時除既不得，爲害更深。」

translations.literal: In Liu Cong's time elimination could not be achieved and the harm was deeper."
translations.idiomatic: In Liu Cong's time elimination could not be achieved and the harm was deeper."

sentences.zh: 仍拒御史，不肯應命。

translations.literal: He still refused the censors and would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: He still refused the censors and would not obey orders.

sentences.zh: 崇大怒，牒報若水曰：「劉聰偽主，德不勝妖；

translations.literal: Chong was greatly angered and replied by dispatch to Ruoshui: "Liu Cong was a false ruler; virtue did not overcome demons;
translations.idiomatic: Chong was greatly angered and replied by dispatch to Ruoshui, "Liu Cong was a false ruler; virtue did not overcome demons;

sentences.zh: 今日聖朝，妖不勝德。

translations.literal: today's sagely court — demons do not overcome virtue.
translations.idiomatic: today's sagely court — demons do not overcome virtue.

sentences.zh: 古之良守，蝗蟲避境，若其修德可免，彼豈無德致然！

translations.literal: Good prefects of antiquity had locusts avoid their borders; if cultivating virtue could avoid them, would they not have had virtue to bring that about!
translations.idiomatic: Good prefects of antiquity had locusts avoid their borders; if cultivating virtue could avoid them, would they not have had virtue to bring that about!

sentences.zh: 今坐看食苗，何忍不救，因以饑饉，將何自安？

translations.literal: Now to sit and watch crops eaten — how can one bear not to save them? When famine follows, how will you be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Now to sit and watch crops eaten — how can one bear not to save them? When famine follows, how will you be at ease?

sentences.zh: 幸勿遲回，自招悔吝。」

translations.literal: I hope you will not delay and invite regret."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will not delay and invite regret."

sentences.zh: 若水乃行焚瘞之法，獲蝗一十四萬石，投汴渠流下者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Ruoshui then carried out burning and burying; locusts obtained were one hundred forty thousand piculs; those cast into the Bian Canal downstream were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui then carried out burning and burying; locusts obtained were one hundred forty thousand piculs; those cast into the Bian Canal downstream were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷喧議，皆以驅蝗爲不便，上聞之，復以問崇。

translations.literal: At that time the court clamored in discussion, all holding driving locusts inconvenient; the emperor heard it and again asked Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court clamored in discussion, all holding driving locusts inconvenient; the emperor heard it and again asked Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「庸儒執文，不識通變。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Mediocre Confucians cling to text and do not know flexible change.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Mediocre Confucians cling to text and do not know flexible change.

sentences.zh: 凡事有違經而合道者，亦有反道而適權者。

translations.literal: In all affairs there are those that violate the classics yet accord with the Way, and also those that go against the Way yet suit expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: In all affairs there are those that violate the classics yet accord with the Way, and also those that go against the Way yet suit expedient power.

sentences.zh: 昔魏時山東有蝗傷稼，緣小忍不除，致使苗稼總盡，人至相食；

translations.literal: In Wei times locusts in Shandong harmed crops; because of small forbearance they were not eliminated, causing crops to be utterly exhausted and men to eat one another;
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times locusts in Shandong harmed crops; because of small forbearance they were not eliminated, causing crops to be utterly exhausted and men to eat one another;

sentences.zh: 後秦時有蝗，禾稼及草木俱盡，牛馬至相啖毛。

translations.literal: later in Qin times there were locusts; grain crops and trees and grass were all exhausted, and cattle and horses even ate one another's hair.
translations.idiomatic: later in Qin times there were locusts; grain crops and trees and grass were all exhausted, and cattle and horses even ate one another's hair.

sentences.zh: 今山東蝗蟲所在流滿，仍極繁息，實所稀聞。

translations.literal: Now locusts in Shandong wherever they are flow full, still extremely prolific — truly rarely heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Now locusts in Shandong wherever they are flow full, still extremely prolific — truly rarely heard of.

sentences.zh: 河北、河南，無多貯積，倘不收獲，豈免流離，事系安危，不可膠柱。

translations.literal: Hebei and Henan have not much stored grain; if harvest is not taken, how can wandering displacement be avoided? The matter concerns safety and danger — one cannot stick to the peg.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei and Henan have not much stored grain; if harvest is not taken, how can wandering displacement be avoided? The matter concerns safety and danger — one cannot stick to the peg.

sentences.zh: 縱使除之不盡，猶勝養以成災。

translations.literal: Even if elimination is not complete, it is still better than nurturing them into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Even if elimination is not complete, it is still better than nurturing them into disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下好生惡殺，此事請不煩出敕，乞容臣出牒處分。

translations.literal: Your Majesty loves life and hates killing; this matter please do not trouble issuing an edict — I beg permission to issue dispatches and handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty loves life and hates killing; this matter please do not trouble issuing an edict — I beg permission to issue dispatches and handle it.

sentences.zh: 若除不得，臣在身官爵，並請削除。」

translations.literal: If elimination cannot be achieved, I request that my present offices and ranks all be struck off."
translations.idiomatic: If elimination cannot be achieved, I request that my present offices and ranks all be struck off."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 黃門監盧懷慎謂崇曰：「蝗是天災，豈可制以人事？

translations.literal: Director of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaishan said to Chong: "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster — how can they be controlled by human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaishan said to Chong, "Locusts are a heaven-sent disaster — how can they be controlled by human affairs?

sentences.zh: 外議鹹以爲非。

translations.literal: Outside opinion all holds it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Outside opinion all holds it wrong.

sentences.zh: 又殺蟲太多，有傷和氣。

translations.literal: Also killing insects is too many — it harms harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Also killing insects is too many — it harms harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 今猶可復，請公思之。」

translations.literal: It can still be reversed — please think again."
translations.idiomatic: It can still be reversed — please think again."

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「楚王吞蛭，厥疾用瘳；

translations.literal: Chong said: "The King of Chu swallowed leeches and his illness was cured;
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "The King of Chu swallowed leeches and his illness was cured;

sentences.zh: 叔敖殺蛇，其福乃降。

translations.literal: Shu'ao killed a snake and his blessing then descended.
translations.idiomatic: Shu'ao killed a snake and his blessing then descended.

sentences.zh: 趙宣至賢也，恨用其犬；

translations.literal: Zhao Xuan was most worthy, yet regretted using his dog;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan was most worthy, yet regretted using his dog;

sentences.zh: 孔丘將聖也，不愛其羊。

translations.literal: Kong Qiu was about to be sage, yet did not spare his sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qiu was about to be sage, yet did not spare his sheep.

sentences.zh: 皆誌在安人，思不失禮。

translations.literal: All recorded intent to settle the people, thinking not to lose ritual.
translations.idiomatic: All recorded intent to settle the people, thinking not to lose ritual.

sentences.zh: 今蝗蟲極盛，驅除可得，若其縱食，所在皆空。

translations.literal: Now locusts are extremely abundant; driving them away can be achieved; if they are allowed to eat, wherever they are will be empty.
translations.idiomatic: Now locusts are extremely abundant; driving them away can be achieved; if they are allowed to eat, wherever they are will be empty.

sentences.zh: 山東百姓，豈宜餓殺！

translations.literal: The people of Shandong — how can they be allowed to starve to death!
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shandong — how can they be allowed to starve to death!

sentences.zh: 此事崇已面經奏定訖，請公勿復爲言。

translations.literal: This matter Chong has already reported face to face and it is settled — please do not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: This matter Chong has already reported face to face and it is settled — please do not speak again.

sentences.zh: 若救人殺蟲，因緣致禍，崇請獨受，義不仰關。」

translations.literal: If saving people by killing insects, through karmic cause brings calamity, Chong requests to bear it alone and will not implicate others."
translations.idiomatic: If saving people by killing insects, through karmic cause brings calamity, Chong requests to bear it alone and will not implicate others."

sentences.zh: 懷慎既庶事曲從，竟亦不敢逆崇之意，蝗因此亦漸止息。

translations.literal: Huaishan, since all affairs bent to follow, ultimately also dared not go against Chong's intent; locusts thereby also gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishan, since all affairs bent to follow, ultimately also dared not go against Chong's intent; locusts thereby also gradually ceased.

sentences.zh: 是時，上初即位，務修德政，軍國庶務，多訪於崇，同時宰相盧懷慎、源乾曜等，但唯諾而已。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne, devoted to cultivating virtuous government; military and state affairs mostly consulted Chong; fellow chancellors Lu Huaishan, Yuan Qianyao and the like only assented.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne, devoted to cultivating virtuous government; military and state affairs mostly consulted Chong; fellow chancellors Lu Huaishan, Yuan Qianyao, and the like only assented.

sentences.zh: 崇獨當重任，明於吏道，斷割不滯。

translations.literal: Chong alone bore heavy responsibility, clear in official ways, decisive without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Chong alone bore heavy responsibility, clear in official ways, decisive without delay.

sentences.zh: 然縱其子光祿少卿彜、宗正少卿異廣引賓客，受納饋遺，由是爲時所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he indulged his sons the Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yi and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Yi in widely receiving guests and accepting presented gifts; thereby he was ridiculed by the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he indulged his sons the Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yi and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Yi in widely receiving guests and accepting presented gifts; thereby he was ridiculed by the times.

sentences.zh: 時有中書主書趙誨爲崇所親信，受蕃人珍遺，事發，上親加鞫問，下獄處死。

translations.literal: At that time the Secretariat chief clerk Zhao Hui was trusted by Chong; he received precious gifts from foreigners; when the matter broke, the emperor personally interrogated him, imprisoned him and put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Secretariat chief clerk Zhao Hui was trusted by Chong; he received precious gifts from foreigners; when the matter broke, the emperor personally interrogated him, imprisoned him, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 崇結奏其罪，復營救之，上由是不悅。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized his crime yet also worked to rescue him; the emperor was thereby displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized his crime yet also worked to rescue him; the emperor was thereby displeased.

sentences.zh: 其冬，曲赦京城，敕文時標誨名，令決杖一百，配流嶺南。

translations.literal: That winter, in a partial amnesty of the capital, the amnesty text at the time marked Hui's name, ordering a hundred blows with the staff and exile to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in a partial amnesty of the capital, the amnesty text at the time marked Hui's name, ordering a hundred blows with the staff and exile to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 崇自是憂懼，頻面陳避相位，薦宋璟皆獲進見。

translations.literal: Chong was thereby anxious and fearful, repeatedly stating face to face his wish to avoid the chancellorship and recommending Song Jing — all obtained audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was thereby anxious and fearful, repeatedly stating face to face his wish to avoid the chancellorship and recommending Song Jing — all obtained audience.

sentences.zh: 有人於洛水中獲自代。

translations.literal: Someone recovered a tally from the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recovered a tally from the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 俄授開府儀同三司，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of Acting with the Same Three Ranks and removed from directing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed grand master of the palace with the honor of acting with the same three ranks and removed from directing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 居月餘，玄宗將幸東都，而太廟屋壞，上召宋璟、蘇颋問其故，璟等奏言：「陛下三年之制未畢，誠不可行幸。

translations.literal: After more than a month the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital, but the ancestral temple hall collapsed; the emperor summoned Song Jing and Su Ting and asked the reason; Jing and the others memorialized: "Your Majesty's three-year mourning is not complete — truly one cannot travel.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital, but the ancestral temple hall collapsed; the emperor summoned Song Jing and Su Ting and asked the reason; Jing and the others memorialized, "Your Majesty's three-year mourning is not complete — truly one cannot travel.

sentences.zh: 凡災變之發，皆所以明教誡。

translations.literal: Whenever calamities and transformations arise, all are to make clear teaching and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever calamities and transformations arise, all are to make clear teaching and admonition.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜增崇大道，以答天意，且停幸東都。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should further exalt the great Way to answer Heaven's intent, and for now stop the visit to the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should further exalt the great Way to answer Heaven's intent, and for now stop the visit to the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 上又召崇問曰：「朕臨發京邑，太廟無故崩壞，恐神靈誡以東行不便耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned Chong and asked: "I was about to depart the capital; the ancestral temple for no reason collapsed — I fear the spirits admonish that going east is inconvenient?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again summoned Chong and asked, "I was about to depart the capital; the ancestral temple for no reason collapsed — I fear the spirits admonish that going east is inconvenient?"

sentences.zh: 崇對曰：「太廟殿本是苻堅時所造，隋文帝創立新都，移宇文朝故殿造此廟，國家又因隋氏舊制，歲月滋深，朽蠹而毀。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "The ancestral temple hall was originally built in Fu Jian's time; Emperor Wen of Sui founded the new capital, moved the old halls of the Yuwen dynasty to build this temple; the state again followed Sui's old system — years and months grew deep, rotted and worm-eaten and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "The ancestral temple hall was originally built in Fu Jian's time; Emperor Wen of Sui founded the new capital, moved the old halls of the Yuwen dynasty to build this temple; the state again followed Sui's old system — years and months grew deep, rotted and worm-eaten and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 山有朽壞，尚不免崩，既久來枯木，合將摧折，偶與行期相會，不是緣行乃崩。

translations.literal: Mountains have rotten decay and still cannot avoid collapse; having long been dead wood, it should be about to break — it happened to coincide with the travel date, not that because of travel it collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains have rotten decay and still cannot avoid collapse; having long been dead wood, it should be about to break — it happened to coincide with the travel date, not that because of travel it collapsed.

sentences.zh: 且四海爲家，兩京相接，陛下以關中不甚豐熟，轉運又有勞費，所以爲人行幸，豈是無事煩勞？

translations.literal: Moreover all within the four seas is home; the two capitals connect — Your Majesty because Guanzhong is not very abundant, and transport also has labor and expense, therefore travels for the people — is it without cause that affairs are troubled?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover all within the four seas is home; the two capitals connect — Your Majesty because Guanzhong is not very abundant, and transport also has labor and expense, therefore travels for the people — is it without cause that affairs are troubled?

sentences.zh: 東都百司已作供擬，不可失信於天下。

translations.literal: The hundred offices of the Eastern Capital have already made preparations — one cannot break faith with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices of the Eastern Capital have already made preparations — one cannot break faith with all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，舊廟既朽爛，不堪修理，望移神主於太極殿安置，更改造新廟，以申誠敬。

translations.literal: In my foolish view, the old temple is rotten and cannot bear repair; I hope the spirit tablets will be moved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate for placement, and a new temple rebuilt, to express sincere respect.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, the old temple is rotten and cannot bear repair; I hope the spirit tablets will be moved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate for placement, and a new temple rebuilt, to express sincere respect.

sentences.zh: 車駕依前徑發。」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage should proceed directly as before."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage should proceed directly as before."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言正合朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words exactly accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words exactly accord with my intent."

sentences.zh: 賜絹二百匹，令所司奉七廟神主於太極殿，改新廟，車駕乃幸東都。

translations.literal: He granted two hundred bolts of silk, ordered the offices to place the seven temple spirit tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, rebuild the new temple, and the imperial carriage then visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He granted two hundred bolts of silk, ordered the offices to place the seven temple spirit tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, rebuild the new temple, and the imperial carriage then visited the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 因令崇五日一參，仍入閤供奉，甚承恩遇。

translations.literal: He then ordered Chong to attend audience every five days, still entering the gate to serve — he received great favor.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Chong to attend audience every five days, still entering the gate to serve — he received great favor.

sentences.zh: 後又除太子少保，以疾不拜。

translations.literal: Later he was again appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; because of illness he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent; because of illness he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 九年薨，年七十二，贈揚州大都督，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, age seventy-two; posthumously appointed Grand General of Yangzhou, posthumous title Wénxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died, age seventy-two; posthumously appointed grand general of Yangzhou, posthumous title Wénxiàn.

sentences.zh: 崇先分其田園，令諸子侄各守其分，仍爲遺令以誡子孫，其略曰：

translations.literal: Chong first divided his fields and gardens, ordered sons and nephews each to keep their share, and also made a testament to admonish descendants; the gist:
translations.idiomatic: Chong first divided his fields and gardens, ordered sons and nephews each to keep their share, and also made a testament to admonish descendants; the gist:

sentences.zh: 比見諸達官身亡以後，子孫既失覆廕，多至貧寒，鬥尺之間，參商是競。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen that after many eminent officials die, their descendants having lost protective shade mostly fall into poverty and cold; over a foot's space they compete like Shang and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have seen that after many eminent officials die, their descendants having lost protective shade mostly fall into poverty and cold; over a foot's space they compete like Shang and Shen.

sentences.zh: 豈唯自玷，乃更辱先，無論曲直，俱受嗤毀。

translations.literal: Not only do they disgrace themselves — they further shame their ancestors; regardless of right and wrong, both receive ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Not only do they disgrace themselves — they further shame their ancestors; regardless of right and wrong, both receive ridicule.

sentences.zh: 莊田水碾，既眾有之，遞相推倚，或致荒廢。

translations.literal: Estate fields and water mills, being jointly owned, push reliance on one another, sometimes causing abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: Estate fields and water mills, being jointly owned, push reliance on one another, sometimes causing abandonment.

sentences.zh: 陸賈、石苞，皆古之賢達也，所以預爲定分，將以絕其後爭，吾靜思之，深所嘆服。

translations.literal: Lu Jia and Shi Bao were both worthy men of antiquity; therefore they beforehand fixed shares, intending to cut off later contention — I ponder this quietly and deeply admire it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia and Shi Bao were both worthy men of antiquity; therefore they beforehand fixed shares, intending to cut off later contention — I ponder this quietly and deeply admire it.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子亞聖，母墓毀而不修；

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius was second only to sage; his mother's tomb was destroyed yet he did not repair it;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Confucius was second only to sage; his mother's tomb was destroyed yet he did not repair it;

sentences.zh: 梁鴻至賢，父亡席卷而葬。

translations.literal: Liang Hong was most worthy; when his father died he buried him wrapped in a mat.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong was most worthy; when his father died he buried him wrapped in a mat.

sentences.zh: 昔楊震、趙咨、盧植、張奐，皆當代英達，通識今古，鹹有遺言，屬以薄葬。

translations.literal: In the past Yang Zhen, Zhao Zi, Lu Zhi and Zhang Huan were all eminent men of their age, broadly knowing past and present; all had dying words, entrusting simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Yang Zhen, Zhao Zi, Lu Zhi, and Zhang Huan were all eminent men of their age, broadly knowing past and present; all had dying words, entrusting simple burial.

sentences.zh: 或濯衣時服，或單帛幅巾，知真魂去身，貴於速朽，子孫皆遵成命，迄今以爲美談。

translations.literal: Some wore clothes just washed, or a single cloth headcloth; knowing the true soul departs the body, valuing quick decay — descendants all followed the completed command; to this day it is considered fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: Some wore clothes just washed, or a single cloth headcloth; knowing the true soul departs the body, valuing quick decay — descendants all followed the completed command; to this day it is considered fine talk.

sentences.zh: 凡厚葬之家，例非明哲，或溺於流俗，不察幽明，鹹以奢厚爲忠孝，以儉薄爲慳惜，至令亡者致戮屍暴骸之酷，存者陷不忠不孝之誚。

translations.literal: All households of lavish burial as a rule are not wise and clear; some are drowned in vulgar custom, not discerning the obscure and bright, all taking lavish thickness as loyal filial piety and taking thrift as stinginess — causing the dead to suffer the cruelty of exposed corpse and hacked body, and the living to fall into the reproach of disloyalty and unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All households of lavish burial as a rule are not wise and clear; some are drowned in vulgar custom, not discerning the obscure and bright, all taking lavish thickness as loyal filial piety and taking thrift as stinginess — causing the dead to suffer the cruelty of exposed corpse and hacked body, and the living to fall into the reproach of disloyalty and unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 可爲痛哉！

translations.literal: It can be lamented!
translations.idiomatic: It can be lamented!

sentences.zh: 可爲痛哉！

translations.literal: It can be lamented!
translations.idiomatic: It can be lamented!

sentences.zh: 死者無知，自同糞土，何煩厚葬，使傷素業。

translations.literal: The dead have no knowledge, the same as dung and soil — why trouble lavish burial and harm plain estate?
translations.idiomatic: The dead have no knowledge, the same as dung and soil — why trouble lavish burial and harm plain estate?

sentences.zh: 若也有知，神不在柩，復何用違君父之令，破衣食之資。

translations.literal: If there is knowledge, the spirit is not in the coffin — why use violating lord and father's command and breaking clothing and food resources?
translations.idiomatic: If there is knowledge, the spirit is not in the coffin — why use violating lord and father's command and breaking clothing and food resources?

sentences.zh: 吾身亡後，可殮以常服，四時之衣，各一副而已。

translations.literal: After my death, one may enshroud in ordinary clothes; seasonal clothes, each one set only.
translations.idiomatic: After my death, one may enshroud in ordinary clothes; seasonal clothes, each one set only.

sentences.zh: 吾性甚不愛冠衣，必不得將入棺墓，紫衣玉帶，足便於身，念爾等勿復違之。

translations.literal: My nature greatly does not love caps and robes — they must not be put into coffin and tomb; purple robe and jade belt suffice on the body — remember you must not again violate this.
translations.idiomatic: My nature greatly does not love caps and robes — they must not be put into coffin and tomb; purple robe and jade belt suffice on the body — remember you must not again violate this.

sentences.zh: 且神道惡奢，冥塗尚質，若違吾處分，使吾受戮於地下，於汝心安乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the spirit way hates extravagance; the dark path values simplicity — if you violate my disposition, making me suffer punishment underground, will your hearts be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the spirit way hates extravagance; the dark path values simplicity — if you violate my disposition, making me suffer punishment underground, will your hearts be at ease?

sentences.zh: 念而思之。

translations.literal: Think and ponder this.
translations.idiomatic: Think and ponder this.

sentences.zh: 今之佛經，羅什所譯，姚興執本，與什對翻。

translations.literal: Today's Buddhist scriptures were translated by Kumarajiva; Yao Xing held the original and faced him in translation.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Buddhist scriptures were translated by Kumarajiva; Yao Xing held the original and faced him in translation.

sentences.zh: 姚興造浮屠於永貴裏，傾竭府庫，廣事莊嚴，而興命不得延，國亦隨滅。

translations.literal: Yao Xing built a pagoda in Yonggui Lane, draining the treasury, broadly making adornment — yet Xing's life could not be extended and the state also followed in perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing built a pagoda in Yonggui Lane, draining the treasury, broadly making adornment — yet Xing's life could not be extended and the state also followed in perishing.

sentences.zh: 又齊跨山東，周據關右，周則多除佛法而修繕兵威，齊則廣置僧徒而依憑佛力。

translations.literal: Also Qi spanned Shandong, Zhou held Guanzhong — Zhou mostly eliminated Buddhism and repaired military might; Qi broadly installed monks and relied on Buddha's power.
translations.idiomatic: Also Qi spanned Shandong, Zhou held Guanzhong — Zhou mostly eliminated Buddhism and repaired military might; Qi broadly installed monks and relied on Buddha's power.

sentences.zh: 及至交戰，齊氏滅亡，國既不存，寺復何有？

translations.literal: When they came to battle, Qi perished — if the state does not exist, what of temples?
translations.idiomatic: When they came to battle, Qi perished — if the state does not exist, what of temples?

sentences.zh: 修福之報，何其蔑如！

translations.literal: The reward of cultivating blessing — how slight!
translations.idiomatic: The reward of cultivating blessing — how slight!

sentences.zh: 梁武帝以萬乘爲奴，胡太后以六宮入道，豈特身戮名辱，皆以亡國破家。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang used ten thousand chariots as a slave; Empress Hu of Northern Wei entered the Way with the six palaces — not only body slaughtered and name shamed, all ended in perishing state and ruined house.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang used ten thousand chariots as a slave; Empress Hu of Northern Wei entered the Way with the six palaces — not only body slaughtered and name shamed, all ended in perishing state and ruined house.

sentences.zh: 近日孝和皇帝發使贖生，傾國造寺，太平公主、武三思、悖逆庶人、張夫人等皆度人造寺，竟術彌街，鹹不免受戮破家，爲天下所笑。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Xiaohé sent envoys to redeem lives, draining the state to build temples; Princess Taiping, Wu Sanzhi, the usurping commoner, Lady Zhang and the like all ordained people and built temples — talismans filled the streets, yet all could not escape slaughter and ruined house, becoming the world's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Emperor Xiaohé sent envoys to redeem lives, draining the state to build temples; Princess Taiping, Wu Sanzhi, the usurping commoner, Lady Zhang, and the like all ordained people and built temples — talismans filled the streets, yet all could not escape slaughter and ruined house, becoming the world's laughter.

sentences.zh: 經云：「求長命得長命，求富貴得富貴」，「刀尋段段壞，火坑變成池。」

translations.literal: The scripture says: 'Seek long life and obtain long life, seek wealth and honor and obtain wealth and honor,' 'Knives seek piece by piece broken, fire pits become ponds.'
translations.idiomatic: The scripture says, 'Seek long life and obtain long life, seek wealth and honor and obtain wealth and honor,' 'Knives seek piece by piece broken, fire pits become ponds.'

sentences.zh: 比求緣精進得富貴長命者爲誰？

translations.literal: Compared to those seeking merit through diligent progress who obtained wealth, honor and long life — who are they?
translations.idiomatic: Compared to those seeking merit through diligent progress who obtained wealth, honor, and long life — who are they?

sentences.zh: 生前易知，尚覺無應，身後難究，誰見有征。

translations.literal: Before death easy to know, yet still felt no response; after death hard to investigate — who has seen proof?
translations.idiomatic: Before death easy to know, yet still felt no response; after death hard to investigate — who has seen proof?

sentences.zh: 且五帝之時，父不葬子，兄不哭弟，言其致仁壽、無夭橫也。

translations.literal: Moreover in the time of the Five Emperors, fathers did not bury sons, elder brothers did not weep younger brothers — speaking of their attaining benevolence and longevity, without untimely violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in the time of the Five Emperors, fathers did not bury sons, elder brothers did not weep younger brothers — speaking of their attaining benevolence and longevity, without untimely violent death.

sentences.zh: 三王之代，國祚延長，人用休息，其人臣則彭祖、老聃之類，皆享遐齡。

translations.literal: In the age of the Three Kings, dynastic fortune extended long, people had rest; their ministers Peng Zu, Laozi and the like all enjoyed far-reaching years.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Three Kings, dynastic fortune extended long, people had rest; their ministers Peng Zu, Laozi, and the like all enjoyed far-reaching years.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，未有佛教，豈抄經鑄像之力，設齋施佛之功耶？

translations.literal: At that time there was not yet Buddhism — was it the power of copying scriptures and casting images, setting feasts and giving to Buddha?
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was not yet Buddhism — was it the power of copying scriptures and casting images, setting feasts and giving to Buddha?

sentences.zh: 《宋書》《西域傳》，有名僧爲《白黑論》，理證明白，足解沈疑，宜觀而行之。

translations.literal: The Song History Western Regions Account has a famous monk's Black and White Treatise — reasoning and evidence clear, sufficient to resolve deep doubt; it should be viewed and followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Song History Western Regions Account has a famous monk's Black and White Treatise — reasoning and evidence clear, sufficient to resolve deep doubt; it should be viewed and followed.

sentences.zh: 且佛者覺也，在乎方寸，假有萬像之廣，不出五蘊之中，但平等慈悲，行善不行惡，則佛道備矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Buddha means awakening, residing in the inch-square heart; though there be the vastness of ten thousand images, none exits the five skandhas; only equal compassion, doing good and not doing evil — then the Buddha-way is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Buddha means awakening, residing in the inch-square heart; though there be the vastness of ten thousand images, none exits the five skandhas; only equal compassion, doing good and not doing evil — then the Buddha-way is complete.

sentences.zh: 何必溺於小説，惑於凡僧，仍將喻品，用爲實錄，抄經寫像，破業傾家，乃至施身亦無所吝，可謂大惑也。

translations.literal: Why must one be drowned in minor tales, confused by ordinary monks, still taking parable items as real records, copying scriptures and writing images, breaking estate and draining house, even giving the body without stint — it can be called great confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Why must one be drowned in minor tales, confused by ordinary monks, still taking parable items as real records, copying scriptures and writing images, breaking estate and draining house, even giving the body without stint — it can be called great confusion.

sentences.zh: 亦有緣亡人造像，名爲追福，方便之教，雖則多端，功德須自發心，旁助寧應獲報？

translations.literal: There are also those who for the dead make images, called pursuing blessing; expedient teaching though has many sides, merit must arise from one's own heart — can assistance by others obtain reward?
translations.idiomatic: There are also those who for the dead make images, called pursuing blessing; expedient teaching though has many sides, merit must arise from one's own heart — can assistance by others obtain reward?

sentences.zh: 遞相欺誑，浸成風俗，損耗生人，無益亡者。

translations.literal: Mutually deceiving, gradually becoming custom, harming the living, without benefit to the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Mutually deceiving, gradually becoming custom, harming the living, without benefit to the dead.

sentences.zh: 假有通才達識，亦爲時俗所拘。

translations.literal: Suppose there are broadly talented and penetrating knowers — they are also bound by vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose there are broadly talented and penetrating knowers — they are also bound by vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 如來普慈，意存利物，損眾生之不足，厚豪僧之有餘，必不然矣。

translations.literal: The Tathagata's universal compassion, intent to benefit things, diminishing the insufficient of the multitude and thickening the surplus of grand monks — surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: The Tathagata's universal compassion, intent to benefit things, diminishing the insufficient of the multitude and thickening the surplus of grand monks — surely cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 且死者是常，古來不免，所造經像，何所施爲？

translations.literal: Moreover the dead is constant; since antiquity unavoidable — scriptures and images made, for what use?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the dead is constant; since antiquity unavoidable — scriptures and images made, for what use?

sentences.zh: 夫釋迦之本法，爲蒼生之大弊，汝等各宜警策，正法在心，勿效兒女子曹，終身不悟也。

translations.literal: Shakyamuni's original Law is the great harm to the blue-black masses — you each should be vigilant; correct Law in the heart — do not imitate boys and girls, never awakening in a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Shakyamuni's original Law is the great harm to the blue-black masses — you each should be vigilant; correct Law in the heart — do not imitate boys and girls, never awakening in a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 吾亡後必不得爲此弊法。

translations.literal: After my death one must not do this harmful Law.
translations.idiomatic: After my death one must not do this harmful Law.

sentences.zh: 若未能全依正道，須順俗情，從初七至終七，任設七僧齋。

translations.literal: If one cannot fully follow the correct Way, one must comply with vulgar feeling; from the first seventh to the final seventh, allow setting seven monk feasts.
translations.idiomatic: If one cannot fully follow the correct Way, one must comply with vulgar feeling; from the first seventh to the final seventh, allow setting seven monk feasts.

sentences.zh: 若隨齋須布施，宜以吾緣身衣物充，不得輒用餘財，爲無益之枉事，亦不得妄出私物，徇追福之虛談。

translations.literal: If following feasts requires giving, use my personal clothing to fulfill it; one must not rashly use other wealth for useless vain affairs, also must not rashly expend private goods, pursuing empty talk of pursuing blessing.
translations.idiomatic: If following feasts requires giving, use my personal clothing to fulfill it; one must not rashly use other wealth for useless vain affairs, also must not rashly expend private goods, pursuing empty talk of pursuing blessing.

sentences.zh: 道士者，本以玄牝爲宗，初無趨競之教，而無識者慕僧家之有利，約佛教而爲業。

translations.literal: Daoists originally take the mysterious female as ancestor; at first there was no teaching of striving for gain; yet the unenlightened admire the profit of Buddhist households and model Buddhism as profession.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists originally take the mysterious female as ancestor; at first there was no teaching of striving for gain; yet the unenlightened admire the profit of Buddhist households and model Buddhism as profession.

sentences.zh: 敬尋老君之説，亦無過齋之文，抑同僧例，失之彌遠。

translations.literal: Respectfully seeking Old Master's teaching, there is also no text of excessive feasts; suppressing it like the monk example, the error goes further.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully seeking Old Master's teaching, there is also no text of excessive feasts; suppressing it like the monk example, the error goes further.

sentences.zh: 汝等勿拘鄙俗，輒屈於家。

translations.literal: You must not be bound by base vulgar custom and rashly bend to the household.
translations.idiomatic: You must not be bound by base vulgar custom and rashly bend to the household.

sentences.zh: 汝等身沒之後，亦教子孫依吾此法云。

translations.literal: After your bodies perish, also teach descendants to follow my method.
translations.idiomatic: After your bodies perish, also teach descendants to follow my method.

sentences.zh: 十七年，重贈崇太子太保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Chong was again posthumously appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Chong was again posthumously appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇長子彜，開元初光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Chong's eldest son Yi, early Kaiyuan Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's eldest son Yi, early Kaiyuan vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 次子異，坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Second son Yi, prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Yi, prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少子弈，少而修謹，開元末，爲禮部侍郎、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Youngest son Yi, in youth cultivated caution; late Kaiyuan Vice Minister of Rites and Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Yi, in youth cultivated caution; late Kaiyuan vice minister of rites and right vice director.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，右相牛仙客薨，彜男閎爲侍御史、仙客判官，見仙客疾亟，逼爲仙客表，請以弈及兵部侍郎盧奐爲宰相代己。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, Right Chancellor Niu Xianke died; Yi's son Hong was Attending Censor and Xianke's case officer; seeing Xianke critically ill, he forced Xianke's memorial requesting Yi and Vice Minister of War Lu Huan as chancellors to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao, Right Chancellor Niu Xianke died; Yi's son Hong was attending censor and Xianke's case officer; seeing Xianke critically ill, he forced Xianke's memorial requesting Yi and Vice Minister of War Lu Huan as chancellors to replace himself.

sentences.zh: 其妻因中使奏之，玄宗聞而怒之，閎決死，弈出爲永陽太守，奐爲臨淄太守。

translations.literal: His wife through a palace envoy reported it; Emperor Xuanzong heard and was angry; Hong was sentenced to death, Yi was sent out as prefect of Yongyang, Huan as prefect of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: His wife through a palace envoy reported it; Emperor Xuanzong heard and was angry; Hong was sentenced to death, Yi was sent out as prefect of Yongyang, Huan as prefect of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 玄孫合，登進士第，授武功尉，遷監察御史，位終給事中。

translations.literal: Great-grandson He, passed the jinshi examination, appointed Wugong District Captain, transferred to Investigating Censor, ended as Director of the Secretariat Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson He, passed the jinshi examination, appointed Wugong district captain, transferred to investigating censor, ended as director of the Secretariat gate.

sentences.zh: 宋璟，邢州南和人，其先自廣平徙焉，後魏吏部尚書弁七代孫也。

translations.literal: Song Jing, a native of Nanhe in Xingzhou; his ancestors moved from Guangping; seventh-generation descendant of Bian, Minister of Personnel of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing, a native of Nanhe in Xing Prefecture; his ancestors moved from Guangping; seventh-generation descendant of Bian, minister of personnel of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 父玄撫，以璟貴，贈邢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xuanfu, because of Jing's eminence, was posthumously appointed prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuanfu, because of Jing's eminence, was posthumously appointed prefect of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 璟少耿介有大節，博學，工於文翰。

translations.literal: Jing in youth was upright with great integrity, broadly learned, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Jing in youth was upright with great integrity, broadly learned, skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，累轉鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination, repeatedly transferred to Draftsman of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination, repeatedly transferred to draftsman of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 當官正色，則天甚重之。

translations.literal: In office he was stern in countenance; Empress Wu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was stern in countenance; Empress Wu greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 長安中，幸臣張易之誣構御史大夫魏元忠有不順之言，引鳳閣舍人張說令證之。

translations.literal: In Chang'an, favored courtier Zhang Yizhi falsely constructed that Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong had disloyal words, and brought in Phoenix Pavilion Draftsman Zhang Shuo to testify.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an, favored courtier Zhang Yizhi falsely constructed that Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong had disloyal words, and brought in Phoenix Pavilion draftsman Zhang Shuo to testify.

sentences.zh: 說將入於御前對覆，惶惑迫懼，璟謂曰：「名義至重，神道難欺，必不可黨邪陷正，以求茍免。

translations.literal: Shuo was about to enter before the emperor for re-examination, fearful and pressed; Jing said to him: "Fame and righteousness are most heavy; the spirit way is hard to deceive — one absolutely cannot join the wicked to trap the upright, seeking careless escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was about to enter before the emperor for re-examination, fearful and pressed; Jing said to him, "Fame and righteousness are most heavy; the spirit way is hard to deceive — one absolutely cannot join the wicked to trap the upright, seeking careless escape.

sentences.zh: 若緣犯顏流貶，芬芳多矣。

translations.literal: If because of offending the countenance one is exiled, fragrant examples are many.
translations.idiomatic: If because of offending the countenance one is exiled, fragrant examples are many.

sentences.zh: 或至不測，吾必叩閤救子，將與子同死。

translations.literal: Or if to the unforeseen, I will knock at the gate to save you and die with you.
translations.idiomatic: Or if to the unforeseen, I will knock at the gate to save you and die with you.

sentences.zh: 努力，萬代瞻仰，在此舉也。」

translations.literal: Strive — ten thousand generations look up; in this act it lies."
translations.idiomatic: Strive — ten thousand generations look up; in this act it lies."

sentences.zh: 說感其言。

translations.literal: Shuo was moved by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was moved by his words.

sentences.zh: 及入，乃保明元忠，竟得免死。

translations.literal: When he entered, he then vindicated Yuanzhong; ultimately obtained escape from death.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered, he then vindicated Yuanzhong; ultimately obtained escape from death.

sentences.zh: 璟尋遷左御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: Jing soon transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Jing soon transferred to left assistant director of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 張易之與弟昌宗縱恣益橫，傾朝附之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi and his brother Changzong grew ever more wanton and overbearing; the whole court attached to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and his brother Changzong grew ever more wanton and overbearing; the whole court attached to them.

sentences.zh: 昌宗私引相工李弘泰觀占吉兇，言涉不順，為飛書所告。

translations.literal: Changzong privately brought in physiognomist Li Hongtai to observe fortune and misfortune; his words touched on disloyalty and he was reported by anonymous letter.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong privately brought in physiognomist Li Hongtai to observe fortune and misfortune; his words touched on disloyalty and he was reported by anonymous letter.

sentences.zh: 璟廷奏請窮究其狀，則天曰：「易之等已自奏聞，不可加罪。」

translations.literal: Jing memorialized at court requesting thorough investigation; Empress Wu said: "Yizhi and the others have already reported themselves — one cannot add crime."
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized at court requesting thorough investigation; Empress Wu said, "Yizhi and the others have already reported themselves — one cannot add crime."

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「易之等事露自陳，情在難恕，且謀反大逆，無容首免。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Yizhi and the others exposed themselves — the feeling is hard to forgive; moreover plotting rebellion and great treason cannot be pardoned at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Yizhi and the others exposed themselves — the feeling is hard to forgive; moreover plotting rebellion and great treason cannot be pardoned at the head.

sentences.zh: 請勒就御史臺勘當，以明國法。

translations.literal: I request ordering investigation at the Censorate to make clear state law.
translations.idiomatic: I request ordering investigation at the censorate to make clear state law.

sentences.zh: 易之等久蒙驅使，分外承恩，臣必知言出禍從，然義激於心，雖死不恨。」

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others long received driving, extraordinarily receiving grace — I surely know words bring disaster following, yet righteousness stirs the heart; though death I do not regret."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and the others long received driving, extraordinarily receiving grace — I surely know words bring disaster following, yet righteousness stirs the heart; though death I do not regret."

sentences.zh: 則天不悅。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 內史楊再思恐忤旨，遽宣敕令璟出。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Zaisi fearing to offend the intent, hastily proclaimed an edict ordering Jing out.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Zaisi, fearing to offend the intent, hastily proclaimed an edict ordering Jing out.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「天顏咫尺，親奉德音，不煩宰臣擅宣王命。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "The imperial countenance is within a foot — personally receiving virtuous words; no need for chief ministers to usurp proclaiming royal command."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "The imperial countenance is within a foot — personally receiving virtuous words; no need for chief ministers to usurp proclaiming royal command."

sentences.zh: 則天意稍解，乃收易之等就臺，將加鞫問。

translations.literal: Empress Wu's intent slightly eased; then Yizhi and the others were taken to the bureau, about to be interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's intent slightly eased; then Yizhi and the others were taken to the bureau, about to be interrogated.

sentences.zh: 俄有特敕原之，仍令易之等詣璟辭謝，璟拒而不見，曰：「公事當公言之，若私見，則法無私也。」

translations.literal: Soon there was a special edict pardoning them; still ordered Yizhi and the others to go to Jing to apologize; Jing refused and would not see them, saying: "Public affairs should be spoken publicly; if private meeting, then law has no private."
translations.idiomatic: Soon there was a special edict pardoning them; still ordered Yizhi and the others to go to Jing to apologize; Jing refused and would not see them, saying, "Public affairs should be spoken publicly; if private meeting, then law has no private."

sentences.zh: 璟嘗侍宴朝堂，時易之兄弟皆為列卿，位三品，璟本階六品，在下。

translations.literal: Jing once attended banquet at the Hall of Morning Audience; at that time the Yizhi brothers were all ranked ministers, third rank; Jing's original rank was sixth rank, below.
translations.idiomatic: Jing once attended banquet at the Hall of Morning Audience; at that time the Yizhi brothers were all ranked ministers, third rank; Jing's original rank was sixth rank, below.

sentences.zh: 易之素畏璟，妄悅其意，虛位揖璟曰：「公第一人，何乃下座？」

translations.literal: Yizhi always feared Jing; falsely pleased his intent, vacated seat and bowed to Jing: "You are first man — why below seat?"
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi always feared Jing; falsely pleased his intent, vacated seat and bowed to Jing, "You are first man — why below seat?"

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「才劣品卑，張卿以為第一人，何也？」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Talent inferior, rank low — Director Zhang takes me as first man — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Talent inferior, rank low — Director Zhang takes me as first man — why?"

sentences.zh: 當時朝列，皆以二張內寵，不名官，呼易之為五郎，昌宗為六郎。

translations.literal: At that time the court array all because the two Zhang had inner favor did not name offices, calling Yizhi Fifth Lord and Changzong Sixth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court array all because the two Zhang had inner favor did not name offices, calling Yizhi Fifth Lord and Changzong Sixth Lord.

sentences.zh: 天官侍郎鄭善果謂璟曰：「中丞奈何呼五郎為卿？」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Bureau of Personnel Zheng Shanguo said to Jing: "Assistant Director, how call Fifth Lord 'you'?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Bureau of Personnel Zheng Shanguo said to Jing, "Assistant Director, how call Fifth Lord 'you'?"

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「以官言之，正當為卿；

translations.literal: Jing said: "Speaking by office, properly should be 'you';
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Speaking by office, properly should be 'you';

sentences.zh: 若以親故，當為張五。

translations.literal: if by kinship, should be Zhang Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: if by kinship, should be Zhang Fifth.

sentences.zh: 足下非易之家奴，何郎之有？

translations.literal: You are not Yi's household slave — what 'lord' is there?
translations.idiomatic: You are not Yi's household slave — what 'lord' is there?

sentences.zh: 鄭善果一何懦哉！」

translations.literal: How cowardly is Zheng Shanguo!"
translations.idiomatic: How cowardly is Zheng Shanguo!"

sentences.zh: 其剛正皆此類也。

translations.literal: His stern uprightness was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His stern uprightness was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 自是易之等常欲因事傷之，則天察其情，竟以獲免。

translations.literal: From this Yizhi and the others often wished to harm him through affairs; Empress Wu perceived their intent and he ultimately escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yizhi and the others often wished to harm him through affairs; Empress Wu perceived their intent and he ultimately escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 中宗嘉璟正直，仍令兼諫議大夫、內供奉，仗下後言朝廷得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong praised Jing's uprightness and still ordered him to concurrently serve as Censor and Palace Attendant; after dismissal from attendance he spoke of court gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong praised Jing's uprightness and still ordered him to concurrently serve as censor and palace attendant; after dismissal from attendance he spoke of court gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 尋拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時武三思恃寵執權，嘗請托於璟，璟正色謂之曰：「當今復子明辟，王宜以侯就第，何得尚幹朝政？

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sanzhi relied on favor and held power; he once requested favors from Jing; Jing sternly said to him: "Today the son is restored and the ruler enlightened — the prince should take a marquisate and go to his residence; how can he still meddle in court politics?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sanzhi relied on favor and held power; he once requested favors from Jing; Jing sternly said to him, "Today the son is restored and the ruler enlightened — the prince should take a marquisate and go to his residence; how can he still meddle in court politics?

sentences.zh: 王獨不見產、祿之事乎？」

translations.literal: Has the prince alone not seen the affair of Chan and Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Has the prince alone not seen the affair of Chan and Lu?"

sentences.zh: 俄有京兆人韋月將上書訟三思潛通宮掖，將為禍患之漸，三思諷有司奏月將大逆不道，中宗特令誅之。

translations.literal: Soon a person of Jingzhao, Wei Yuejiang, memorialized accusing Sanzhi of secret communication with the inner palace, the gradual approach of calamity; Sanzhi prompted the relevant offices to memorialize Yuejiang for great treason; Emperor Zhongzong specially ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a person of Jingzhao, Wei Yuejiang, memorialized accusing Sanzhi of secret communication with the inner palace, the gradual approach of calamity; Sanzhi prompted the relevant offices to memorialize Yuejiang for great treason; Emperor Zhongzong specially ordered execution.

sentences.zh: 璟執奏請按其罪狀，然後申明典憲，月將竟免極刑，配流嶺南而死。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized requesting investigation according to his crimes, then declaring canonical punishment; Yuejiang ultimately escaped extreme punishment, exiled to Lingnan and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized requesting investigation according to his crimes, then declaring canonical punishment; Yuejiang ultimately escaped extreme punishment, exiled to Lingnan and died.

sentences.zh: 中宗幸西京，令璟權檢校并州長史，未行，又帶本官檢校貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong visited the Western Capital, ordered Jing to act as chief administrator of Bingzhou; before departing, again with his original office acting as chief administrator of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong visited the Western Capital, ordered Jing to act as chief administrator of Bingzhou; before departing, again with his original office acting as chief administrator of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河北頻遭水潦，百姓饑餒，三思封邑在貝州，專使征其租賦，璟又拒而不與，由是為三思所擠。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei repeatedly suffered floods; the people were hungry; Sanzhi's enfeoffment was in Beizhou; he specially sent envoys to levy his rent and tax; Jing again refused and would not give — thereby he was squeezed by Sanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hebei repeatedly suffered floods; the people were hungry; Sanzhi's enfeoffment was in Beizhou; he specially sent envoys to levy his rent and tax; Jing again refused and would not give — thereby he was squeezed by Sanzhi.

sentences.zh: 又歷杭、相二州刺史，在官清嚴，人吏莫有犯者。

translations.literal: He also served as prefect of Hang and Xiang; in office he was pure and stern; officials and people had none who offended.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as prefect of Hang and Xiang; in office he was pure and stern; officials and people had none who offended.

sentences.zh: 中宗晏駕，拜洛州長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong died, he was appointed chief administrator of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong died, he was appointed chief administrator of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，遷吏部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he transferred to Minister of Personnel and Associate Director of the Secretariat, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he transferred to minister of personnel and associate director of the Secretariat, third rank.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在春宮，又兼右庶子，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; he was again Concurrent Right Vice Director and Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; he was again concurrent right vice director and silver-gleam grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，外戚及諸公主干預朝政，請托滋甚。

translations.literal: Previously, maternal relatives and various princesses intervened in court politics; requests for favors grew extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, maternal relatives and various princesses intervened in court politics; requests for favors grew extreme.

sentences.zh: 崔湜、鄭愔相次典選，為權門所制，九流失敘，預用兩年員闕註擬，不足，更置比冬選人，大為士庶所嘆。
